topic: Codexify the fleet cockpit roster + zoomed-agent view (inline-flow scrollback)
notes:
CONTEXT (done): The standalone single-agent view (`bro agent`) now uses codex's inline-flow model — vendored custom_terminal (dynamic inline viewport) + slim insert_history (scroll-region insertion) — so its transcript flows into the terminal's REAL scrollback (tmux/mouse/copy-mode scroll & select natively, like codex CLI). Shipped on beta/blackbox-v2 (commits 93cd97a..5fdd1fe). The shared rendering lifts (snapshot net, monolith split, word-wrapping, syntect highlighting, md-fence-unwrap) also landed. The fleet cockpit (`bro fleet`, run_tui_inner) was DELIBERATELY left on the alt-screen full-paint model.

REMAINING WORK to codexify the roster/cockpit:

1) Zoomed single-agent view → inline-flow with alt/inline mode-switching. When you zoom into an agent (→) in the cockpit, that transcript should flow into scrollback like the standalone view does. Use codex's enter/leave_alt_screen pattern: roster = alt-screen dashboard; zoom-in switches to the inline viewport loop; zoom-out restores alt-screen. run_tui_inner_inline is the working template; the committed/active split + insert_history are already built and reusable. The hard part is the mode TRANSITION (clearing, viewport handoff).

2) Per-agent commit cursors. Standalone has ONE agent (App.committed / committed_initial). The cockpit has N agents; committed state must be per-agent. Switching the zoomed agent must handle scrollback: you can't interleave two agents' histories in one terminal scrollback — likely clear scrollback (or print a separator banner) on zoom-to-different-agent and reset that agent's cursor.

3) Roster list rendering (draw_roster). The roster is a live dashboard, NOT a linear transcript, so inline-flow does not apply to it — it stays alt-screen. Apply codex rendering polish + a scroll affordance (ratatui Scrollbar / position %) if the roster exceeds the screen.

4) Scroll ergonomics (deferred from the earlier codex analysis): position affordance (scrollbar or '↑N · x%'), half-page keys — for remaining in-app-scroll surfaces (roster list; any non-inline view). Mouse-wheel stays an intentional non-goal (conflicts with native terminal selection; codex declined it too) unless we add in-app selection.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS to carry into the cockpit work:
- Resize/reflow: committed scrollback lines are wrapped at commit-time width; on terminal resize they do NOT reflow (codex's transcript_reflow.rs state machine was NOT ported). Acceptable for v1; revisit if painful.
- ≤1-frame commit-boundary transient: as a turn finalizes and content moves from the live viewport into scrollback, a sub-100ms frame can be momentarily unpainted (self-corrects next redraw). Imperceptible live.

REFERENCES:
- Template: run_tui_inner_inline + commit_inline_history + drain_tui_events in crates/bro-cli/src/fleet_tui.rs.
- Primitives: crates/bro-cli/src/fleet_tui/custom_terminal.rs (dynamic viewport) + insert_history.rs (scroll-region insertion).
- Codex pattern: codex-rs/tui/src/tui.rs enter_alt_screen / leave_alt_screen.
- Design: design/fleet-tui/ (cockpit + standalone-view docs).

DEFECT (found while validating the fleet-tui status fixes): brodex multi-turn steering produces NO output — a real defect, not by-design one-shot.

Findings (code-grounded):
- Post-§7, ALL fleet providers are one-shot-per-dispatch; multi-turn rides RESUME (relaunch `--resume <session_id> -p <text>`), NOT a persistent stdin session. See bro-fleet-client/src/fleet.rs:296-300 — can_steer() requires TaskStatus::Running, which is false once a turn finishes, so steer_selected → resume_agent for every provider.
- glm steering works (tmux-verified) → the resume path is sound for the Anthropic stream-json transport.
- brodex IS bidi/steerable (provider_supports_bidi includes Brodex; it's a default cockpit provider) but its resume yields no output → the defect is specifically in the brodex resume leg.

Root-cause candidates in the harness resume path (bro-harness/src/agent_loop.rs:570-607):
  (a) "resume transport mismatch" bail at line 601 if the persisted session transport name != the transport the resumed harness builds from env. brodex is UNIQUELY on the OpenAI Responses transport (the rest are Anthropic), so it's the only provider exposed to a dispatch-vs-resume transport-name mismatch.
  (b) No session file persisted for the Responses session (see note at line 356) → resume finds nothing → context-less (would still produce output, so less likely given the no-output symptom).
  (c) brodex session_id not captured into the fleet snapshot → resume_agent (fleet_tui.rs:2251) short-circuits with "no session id — can't resume".
resume_env_overrides (fleet_tui/dispatch.rs:440) sets only worktree/cargo env; the transport is resolved daemon-side via brofile::resolve_provider_env by provider — a provider/transport-resolution gap on the RESUME leg (vs dispatch) is the most likely culprit.

DEFINITIVE NEXT STEP: reproduce `bro agent --provider brodex "<prompt>"`, let the turn finish, submit a second steer; read the daemon/harness log to see which of (a)/(b)/(c) fires; fix at that seam; validate a second brodex turn produces output AND retains prior context.

Repro observed: working→complete with no new output on the 2nd turn (brodex); glm 2nd turn works.

Related status fixes already shipped on beta/blackbox-v2 (commits 5fdd1fe..1b3588e): inline composer/viewport residue, static "took Xs" turn duration, and "working Ns" shown for the full turn (incl. non-streaming brodex) via treating pending_inputs as active.

RESOLUTION of Note 2 (brodex multi-turn steering "defect"): NOT A REAL RESUME/TRANSPORT DEFECT. Root-cause candidates (a) transport-mismatch bail, (b) no session file, (c) session_id not captured — all FALSIFIED by direct experiment. brodex multi-turn steering works on the current installed build (1b3588e). Verified two independent ways:

1) Server-side (control plane): brodex first turn via POST /control/exec (session 338cc1a8) → "BRODEX-FIRST"; then POST /control/resume with the fleet client's exact resume_body shape (provider, session_id, prompt, allow_recursion, project_dir — fleet.rs:982) → "BRODEX-SECOND. Before, I said BRODEX-FIRST." Output produced AND prior context retained. The daemon/harness resume leg (bro_resume → resolve_resume_target → in-process harness) is sound for the OpenAI Responses transport.

2) Real TUI (tmux, isolated socket): `bro agent --provider brodex "Reply exactly: TUI-FIRST"`, let turn finish, typed 2nd turn in composer + Enter → "✣ working" shown for the full turn → "TUI-SECOND. Before, I said: TUI-FIRST." rendered with context retained, static "✓ took 15s".

EXPLANATION: The original symptom ("working→complete with no new output on the 2nd turn") was a manifestation of the STATUS-DISPLAY bugs, observed while validating those very fixes. Eliminated by 774da8f (inline composer/viewport residue + static turn duration) and 1b3588e (show "working" for the whole turn incl. non-streaming providers via treating pending_inputs as active). Before 1b3588e a non-streaming provider's resumed turn could momentarily read as "complete" with the output not yet/again painted; the fix made the working state cover the full turn and the transcript repaint correctly. No code change needed for the resume path.

PROCESS NOTE: dispatched bro 22d00e3e (brodex) did a thorough but misdirected harness-side code walk and hit its 50-turn cap before running the decisive 2nd-turn experiment. The experiment (resume an already-completed brodex session and check for output+context) is what settled it — both server-side and in the real TUI. Probe tasks pruned; tmux repro session killed. Note 2's "DEFINITIVE NEXT STEP" is now closed: resume produces output and retains context.

PROGRESS (commit fa09761 on beta/fleet-tui-codexify): Note-1 items 1 & 2 DONE — cockpit zoomed view now uses inline-flow.

- Item 1 (zoom→inline-flow + alt/inline mode-switch): implemented as a loop-of-loops at run_tui_cockpit alternating run_roster_view (alt-screen dashboard) ↔ run_inline_view (inline flow on main screen). Zoom-in (→) leaves alt + flows the focused agent into real scrollback; zoom-out (←) restores alt-screen roster. Raw mode owned by run_tui_cockpit across both.
- Item 2 (per-agent commit cursors): App.committed/committed_initial → inline_commits: HashMap<task_id, InlineCommit>. run_inline_view generalized from hard-wired idx-0/len==1 to inline_focus_idx(app) (standalone→agent 0; cockpit→focused_agent_id). On zoom-in the screen+scrollback are hard-purged (clear_scrollback_and_visible_screen_ansi) and the focused agent's cursor reset, so a different agent never interleaves. Entry seeds a correctly-sized viewport (inline_seed_viewport) before the first commit — without it the whole-transcript commit ran against a full-screen viewport (top()==0 → degenerate \x1b[1;0r scroll region) and left the tail as residue in the composer rows.

Validated via tmux (isolated socket, real cockpit, 80x24): zoom-in flows clean (no composer residue), zoom-out clean roster (alt=1), switching vbh↔bdx purges+reflows with zero interleaving (verified by marker grep in scrollback both directions), standalone `bro agent` unchanged. 69 fleet_tui tests pass, clippy clean.

KEY LEARNING for future capture-based validation: tmux capture-pane includes MAIN-screen scrollback above alt-screen content, which looks like roster residue but isn't — use `tmux -S <sock> capture-pane -p` (visible-only) and `display-message -p '#{alternate_on}'` to disambiguate. Detached tmux sessions default to 80x24 regardless of resize-pane.

REMAINING (Note 1): item 3 (roster scroll affordance — Table already auto-scrolls to selection, needs a visible scrollbar/'↑N·x%'), item 4 (half-page PgUp/PgDn for the roster). Known limitation unchanged: committed scrollback does not reflow on resize.

SESSION PROGRESS (commits fa09761, c57924a, cc295ec, f91939f, 64fd627 on beta/blackbox-v2 + beta/fleet-tui-codexify; release bro + release daemon deployed):

NOTE-1 ITEMS DONE:
- Item 1+2 (zoom→inline-flow + per-agent commit cursors): fa09761. Cockpit zoom flows the focused agent into real scrollback; loop-of-loops run_tui_cockpit ↔ run_roster_view/run_inline_view; per-agent inline_commits map; clean purge+reflow on agent switch (no interleaving). tmux-validated.
- Item 3+4 (roster scroll affordance + half-page keys): c57924a. PgUp/PgDn half-page (clamped), Home/End, "▾ pos/total · pct%" on overflow.
- RESIZE/REFLOW (was the deferred known-limitation): cc295ec. On any size change the inline views purge + re-flow the whole transcript at the new size (require correct rewrap; height-shrink duplicate-border fixed). Validated live: standalone 110↔60 re-wraps + rebuilds scrollback; cockpit zoom width/height/combined all clean.
- ERGONOMICS pass: f91939f. Esc in selectors now cancels to roster (was quitting the whole cockpit); deepseek selector spacing; help overlay auto-fits + new paging keys + native-scroll line; `?` is a normal char in the inline agent view (was setting an unrenderable overlay that ate the next key).

DAEMON WEDGE (separate mission, ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED + DEPLOYED): 64fd627. The prod daemon (com.daystrom.blackbox) had wedged — root cause: the in-process harness's glob/content_search tools (bro_tools::workspace) walk the dispatch cwd with ignore::WalkBuilder, which only honors .gitignore when it detects a git repo via a .git DIRECTORY. This checkout is a linked git WORKTREE (.git is a file/gitdir pointer), so detection failed and the walk descended into the gitignored 30GB target/ (65k files); concurrent in-process dispatches thrashed disk + piled up on the index RwLock → wedge (diagnosed via live sample(1): workers in RawRwLock::lock_shared_slow, holder in Glob→walkdir inside target). Fix: hardened_walk() with require_git(false) + filter_entry pruning build/VCS dirs (target, node_modules, .git, …) + regression test. Rebuilt+restarted prod daemon (authorized); validated glob in the 30GB worktree now returns in 13s and the daemon stays responsive. This also explains the earlier bbox_thread hangs (same wedged daemon).

REMAINING (Note 1): none of the original 4 items; the only deferred item (resize reflow) is now done. Optional future polish: roster bucket-label paren clips at very narrow widths (≤70 cols).
